look_here_first: For CANADA goldenrod, compare the mid-stem leaf TOOTH pattern and the lower/upper stem hairs with S. altissima; Canada commonly has finer, often more regularly toothed thinner 3-nerved leaves and sparser/longer stem hair than tall goldenrod. However overlap is extreme and some variants of both break these patterns. S. gigantea is the smoother/waxy lower stem one. Photograph lower stem, an entire leaf face/underside and flowering branches on SAME plant.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Alternate, lanceolate, serrate, 3-nerved, generally thinner/less harsh than S. altissima.

key_traits.label: Heads
key_traits.text: Many small yellow heads in plume-like terminal inflorescences.

key_traits.label: Best field traits
key_traits.text: golden plume inflorescences; narrower leaves; compare with S. altissima for roughness/robustness
